proofs.text: Call `tag_validated()` with two record paths; verify `git cat-file tag validated/<name>` prints an annotated tag whose message lists both paths one per line, that a later prune keeps the older record those paths name, and that `validated_paths()` returns an empty set outside a git repository

rule_text: `purlin:verify --tag <name>` writes the annotated tag `validated/<name>` listing one record path per line in its message, and retention never deletes a path any `validated/*` message names

tests.body:
def test_a_validated_tag_keeps_the_records_its_message_names(project):
    oldest = put_record(project, 'greeting',
                        '20260101T120000Z-4f1c2ab-ci.json')
    for day in range(11, 16):
        put_record(project, 'greeting',
                   '202609%dT120000Z-4f1c2ab-ci.json' % day)
    git(project, 'add', '-A')
    git(project, 'commit', '--quiet', '-m', 'records')
    records_module.tag_validated(project, '1.0', [oldest])

    assert records_module.validated_paths(project) == {oldest}
    records_module.prune(project, 'greeting')
    kept = names(project, 'greeting')
    assert os.path.basename(oldest) in kept
    assert len(kept) == 4, 'the newest three plus the one the tag names'
tests.name: test_a_validated_tag_keeps_the_records_its_message_names
